title: Reduce host-side overhead in prefill/decode pipeline to cut tail latency and CPU utilization
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: In production traces for high-concurrency text-generation workloads, a non-trivial fraction (20-35%) of end-to-end tail latency and a large portion of host CPU utilization are attributed to host-side activities: synchronous host->GPU memory copies during prefill/decode, GPU stream synchronization, and contention in the runtime threadpool used for batching and IO. This ticket scopes an initiative to systematically reduce host overhead by changing memory copy strategies, improving CPU-GPU overlap, and reducing threadpool contention in the prefill/decode scheduling path.

Goals: (1) Decrease 95th and 99th percentile latency for 2K token/response workloads by 15-25% on p4d/p3-equivalent hardware, (2) Reduce host CPU utilization per GPU by 20% under peak throughput, (3) Maintain or improve token-per-second throughput and model quality.

Background & Observations:
- Current runtime uses blocking cudaMemcpy for prefill chunk uploads and small synchronous copies during decode when evicting/refreshing KV cache segments.
- Prefill and decode scheduling are coordinated by a shared threadpool that also handles RPC, batching and diagnostics—leading to priority inversion during load spikes.
- Kernel selection optimizations already reduce compute time, but host overhead prevents full utilization of potential GPU throughput improvements.

Approach / Proposed changes:
1) Replace synchronous host->device copies for prefill with pinned host buffers and asynchronous cuMemcpy/streams to overlap host staging with kernel execution. Use a small pool of pre-registered pinned buffers sized to typical chunk sizes.
2) Introduce per-GPU CUDA stream pools and ensure each prefill/decode task uses non-default streams to avoid implicit synchronization. Add stream tagging for tracing and metrics.
3) Implement zero-copy staging for small attention KV updates where possible (cudaHostRegister + map) to eliminate one memcpy in the hot path. Fallback to async copy for larger segments.
4) Reduce threadpool contention by splitting the runtime threadpool into two: a lightweight IO/transport pool (short jobs) and a compute-coordinator pool (prefill/decode orchestration). Use lock-free task queues and bounded work-stealing to avoid spikes.
5) Introduce an arena allocator for temporary host buffers to avoid frequent malloc/free on hot path. Bind allocator to NUMA nodes matching GPU affinity.
6) Add new kernel selection heuristic that factors in expected host overlap (penalize kernels that require synchronous host transfers).
7) Extend telemetry to capture per-request memcpy time, stream synchronization stalls, threadpool queue times, and host CPU steal metrics.

Risks / Trade-offs:
- Pinned memory increases overall host RAM footprint; must cap pool size and use eviction heuristics.
- More async behavior complicates error handling and shutdown. Add explicit cleanup paths and timeouts.
- NUMA and GPU affinity improvements add OS/hardware-specific complexity and increase test matrix.

Planned experiments & benchmarks:
- Baseline: 2K token chat benchmark used for runtime-2.2 perf numbers (p95: 640ms, p99: 880ms, host CPU 78% avg).
- Experiment A: Pinned async memcpy + stream pooling. Measure p95/p99 and host CPU.
- Experiment B: Add threadpool split + arena allocator. Measure queue latency reduction and effective concurrency.
- Experiment C: Add zero-copy path for small KV updates and kernel selection heuristic. Evaluate failure/fallback rate and memory overhead.
Acceptance criteria: p95 latency reduction >= 15% on 2K token workload compared to baseline runtime-2.2
host CPU utilization per GPU reduced by >= 20% at target load
telemetry for memcpy/stream/queue included in runtime metrics and surfaced in Console dashboard
implementation covered by unit and integration tests; graceful fallback on OS/hardware without pinned memory support
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Martinez: Spiked an async memcpy prototype on devbox gcp-p4d; initial run shows 12% p95 drop but increased RSS due to pinned buffers. Need eviction policy. (link to logs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DevSpikeLogs)

2026-03-04 - Devon Chen: Threadpool profiling shows >40% of CPU time in scheduler locks under 400 concurrent requests. Proposal: split pools and use lock-free queues. See flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/inference/flame/ENG-4821/2026-03-04
2026-03-06 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Prioritize minimizing memory footprint; propose soft cap on pinned pool with LRU eviction and fall back to async memcpy if over threshold.
2026-03-09 - Design review (Luca Rossi): Streaming state needs explicit UX for diagnostics; added metric tags and correlation IDs in streaming payloads.
2026-03-11 - Security: Verified cudaHostRegister usage acceptable; recommend auditing for zero-copy path and ensuring no sensitive data stays pinned longer than needed.

2026-03-13 - Devon Chen: Implemented initial async copy + stream pool in branch runtime/async-copies (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1024). Running canary against internal loadgen now.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flagged changes behind runtime.config.host_overhead_opt_in. 2) Canary on dedicated cluster with 10% of traffic for 48 hours, monitor memcpy/stream/queue metrics and error rates. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% and then 100% over 7 days if no regressions. 4) If increased OOM or degraded latency, automatic rollback via canary controller and alert on Console.
